p: Distribution-fitted pixel-signal estimation and auto-stretch for PixInsight. NukeX works on the FITS light frames you add (with optional flats): for every pixel it fits a statistical distribution to every pixel's samples across the stack, estimates the signal from the fitted model, and applies one of its stretches (Auto is recommended). A camera quantum-efficiency (QE) database built into the module routes each frame and decomposes dual-narrowband colour data (HaO3 / S2O3) into emission lines. Frames open only as local files, and the FITS library has no network or shared-memory drivers. New in 5.3.1.3: Pause/Abort during the final post-processing (coverage trim, sky-gradient removal, local noise measurement, dual-narrowband line separation, noise check) is seen within a fraction of a second; on ten 24-megapixel frames on a busy machine it could wait 12-36 s. Every stack is unchanged. Also recent: Pause/Abort during distribution fitting is seen within a few hundredths of a second (it waited up to 1.2 s), Pause/Abort while frames are measured no longer waits for star detection on frames where a bright nebula fills the field (it took 14-20 s; now about half a second), flats from a colour (OSC) camera are applied to each pixel by its own colour before debayering, the Lupton stretch gives its linear limit at Q = 0 and refuses a stretch value of 0, and CLAHE's per-channel mode equalizes every channel of a colour image. Built for PixInsight 1.9.6 / PCL 2.13; requires PixInsight 1.9.6 or later. It loads on any Linux with glibc 2.34 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Rocky/RHEL 9+).

Network: one kind of connection only, the camera-database update check. It makes HTTPS requests to raw.githubusercontent.com (this repository), automatically at most once every 7 days when you open the NukeX window, and whenever you press Check now; it sends no identifier, usage data or image data. A newer database is downloaded and installed only if you agree, after its Ed25519 signatures are verified. Automatic checks can be turned off in the NukeX window. NukeX launches no external program. Files outside the PixInsight installation: ~/.config/nukex4/ (update-check state, a downloaded database, filter names you teach it, your stretch ratings), a frame cache in ~/.cache/nukex4/cache/ while a run lasts, and, while a run lasts, its progress files in a private directory (mode 0700) under $TMPDIR or /tmp, deleted when the run ends. Documentation, including every network connection, external program and file location: doc/tools/NukeX/NukeX.html.
